To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the titration technique is a powerful tool to investigate the interactions between solutes in multicomponent systems; (2) the titration experiments are usually conducted in a diluted solution; (3) the thermodynamic partial properties of the solutes can be determined by the titration experiments using different experimental techniques; and (4) the titration results can provide useful thermodynamic data for the design of separation processes in multicomponent system.

(1) the partial molar volume and the partial adiabatice compressibility of solutes can be determined by titration experiments with densimetry and sound speed measurement, and (2) the partial molarity and the partial isothermal compressibility of solute can be determined by the titration experiments with the isothermal titration microcalorimetry.

(1) the partial volumes and partial isentropic compressibilities of the solutes are determined by titration technique, (2) the partial volumes are determined by titrating the solute with a non-solvent and (3) the partial isentropic (or adiabatic) compressibilities are obtained by titrating the solution with a solvent (non-solvent).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theoretical framework to describe the thermodynamic properties of a mixture of solute and solvent.
the thermodynamic properties of multicomponent solutions.

the determination of thermodynamic partial properties in multicomponent systems, such as partial volumes, partial adiabat compressibilities, partial heat capacities, partial enthalpies, partial entropies, partial Gibbs energies, partial solvation energies, and partial transfer energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the titration techniques provide a useful and reliable tool to determine the thermodynamic partial properties in diluted solutions of multicomponent systems.
, for the determination of partial properties by the titration techniques, a rigorous thermodynamic analysis is required.
the partial properties are not only useful to characterize the interactions of solutes but also to understand the molecular mechanisms involved in the solvation processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamic partial properties can be determined with a high degree of accuracy and that the results are consistent with those obtained by other methods.
the titration techniques can be applied to determine partial thermodynamic properties in multicomponent systems.
the partial properties of a solute are not additive in a mixture, even for non interacting species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the titration technique can be used as a thermodynamic tool for studying the interaction between solute molecules in a solution.
the partial thermodynamic properties can be determined from a single titration curve.
, when a titrant is added to a solvent, a new solvent is generated, and the thermodynamic properties of this solvent can be determined.
